title: XRmuseum Prototype Design and Technical Note
subtitle: COMP5424 Extended Reality | Group 2 | 18 October 2026 | Final build update
version: Prototype and ZIP source 6088c736 | Editor suites at 024d039

blocks.text: XRmuseum is a Windows PC VR maritime gallery centred on diving helmets. The core question is whether visitors can inspect an unfamiliar object and explain its connections to surface air and communication equipment. Phase 2 concentrates on a testable exploration journey. Seated access and operation with one controller are team design hypotheses: the client has not confirmed a priority audience or minimum accessibility specification. [1,2]
Visitor journey

Enter and choose a language; approach the central exhibit; rotate it, inspect a window or cutaway, and select component explanations; optionally compare eras and AIR/VOICE demonstrations; restore the exhibit or viewpoint and leave. The left-plinth photo study is optional. Exploration has no compulsory order, time limit or knowledge score. A visited mark records exposure to content, not understanding.

rows: Museum context and credible content
Maritime gallery; central early, Mark V and SuperLite studies; separate 1988 photo study. Interpretive mechanisms are qualified. [3,5,6]
Model estimates remain; right-plinth expansion is deferred.
Principal XR exploration
Fixed-centre rotation, inspection window, fixed cutaway slider, three component hotspots and optional equipment demonstrations. [4]
Manipulation is implemented; learning benefit is unmeasured.
Reduced motor demand
Single-controller exhibit manipulation, ray/direct selection, precision rotation and adjustable viewing height. [4]
Complete single-controller navigation and seated reach are unverified.
Information access
Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and English; hover outlines and visited checks; captions, sound toggle and reduced motion. [4,12]
Translation quality, binocular reading and sensory coverage need evaluation.
Guidance and recovery
Contextual hints, press/release feedback, move-away cancellation, exhibit RESET and separate RESET VIEW. [4]
Legacy NEW VISIT is hidden in the default interface.
Evaluable delivery
Public repository, six member identities, source, Windows ZIP and version-bound reports. [3,7,9,11]
Build/package checks passed; PQ604 and headset acceptance remain pending.

blocks.text: Course expectations concern a coherent journey, principal XR behaviour, recovery and delivery. Motor and information provisions are this team's selected responses, not a client-approved checklist or evidence of universal accessibility. [1,2]

MuseumStart is the enabled build scene. Unity 2022.3.62f3c1, OpenXR 1.14.3, XRI 2.6.4, Input System 1.14.0 and URP 14.0.12 provide the PC VR foundation. The Editor simulator gate retains physical headset input when a real XR device is present. Runtime features live under Assets/Museum/Features; input adapters, interaction coordination, exhibit state and presentation have separate responsibilities. [3]
Constrain manipulation and preserve state

HelmetDiegeticStation reuses the inspection, era and demonstration engines while replacing default free grabbing with rotation around a fixed centre. A fixed slider changes cut depth. This reduces translation and coordination demands at the cost of free handling; its accessibility benefit is a hypothesis. Earlier two-hand grabbing and FLOAT remain a development configuration when the station is disabled. They are not simultaneously available in the default visitor mode. [4]

Gesture controls stop on release. Diegetic and left-plinth buttons confirm on release at the original target; moving away cancels. Cross-target release guards and cancellation before view recovery guard against accidental commands. After the left exhibit was added, its buttons gained solid-occlusion checks during selection, holding and release: a cone-assisted target alone did not prove an unobstructed interaction. [6]
Coordinate models and information

Era profiles and an event channel drive distinct early, Mark V and SuperLite geometries. RefinedHelmetBinding updates visible renderers, window triggers, section data and demonstration endpoints; HelmetEraVisitorContent aligns captions and hotspots with the model actually applied. Inspection Shell and Glass shaders preserve cutaway and hover effects. This avoids a colour-only change or a caption announcing geometry that has not appeared. [3,5]

The language channel is the single source of language state. Static labels bind to keys; dynamic text uses MuseumText.Set. Saved translation tables and baked TMP glyphs are checked alongside runtime text. Contextual hints and a summonable settings/about panel reduce permanent clutter. The panel faces the viewer once, then stays fixed; it checks visible bounds and obstacles, including the left exhibit. Placement may be refused when no suitable space exists. [4,12]
Keep interpretation distinguishable

The early model references Science Museum Group object 1881-47; the 1988 photo study is a separate object. Unseen geometry, some dimensions and material choices are estimates. The early moving panel and SuperLite side-opening window are teaching aids, while air routes, signal timing and synthetic sounds include interpretation. The left gallery offers only 30-degree rotation, reset and qualified labels; section preview belongs to an isolated comparison scene. Editable sources, exports and Unity copies retain their provenance and GUIDs. [5,6,11]

The prototype and ZIP use repository revision 6088c736, including the left exhibit. Its committed MuseumVR tree is identical to frozen Editor validation source 024d039 (tree eaa3237d). The table retains archived suite results; those suites were not rerun for this update. The new build used a clean worktree, excluding the pre-existing local ProjectSettings change. [3,6,7,9]

blocks.text: Each Editor process exited naturally with code 0 and left 1,299 project files unchanged. Synthetic devices exercised production Input Actions in saved scenes. Counts include repeated text, glyph and fingerprint assertions; they are not participants or independent usability tasks and must not be summed. Monocular captures do not establish binocular readability or physical reach. [7]

Historical runs at 7e5b539 include 31 direct-contact checks for the default era and specified surfaces, and 318 isolated-comparison checks. Comparison inputs are unchanged, but that suite was not rerun after left-plinth integration; coverage remains version-specific. [8]
Build and real-device evidence

A clean 6088c736 Windows x64 Development/Mono build on 18 October succeeded with zero errors and two existing optional OpenXR warnings; the Editor exited naturally with code 0. All 1,299 project files remained unchanged. The ZIP contains 272 Unity outputs plus instructions and a manifest: 274 files, 74,726,292 bytes. CRC and extracted-file SHA-256 checks passed. [9]

The extracted Player completed a 40-second local startup observation: Mono, D3D11, input and scene scripts initialized without unexpected managed exceptions. No headset was available; OpenXR reported XR_ERROR_FORM_FACTOR_UNAVAILABLE. The hidden-window probe ended by terminating its own Player process (exit -1). Natural Player shutdown, stereo rendering and VR interaction were not verified. PQ604 acceptance remains pending. [9]

Earlier Quest 3/Virtual Desktop feedback reported improved head rotation/viewing height and, in an earlier hand build, grabbing, hand-gap and joystick problems. Later repairs still need a complete headset retest. This is formative developer feedback, not participant research or approval of compatibility with the course’s SteamVR/Meta Quest Link lab environment. [2,10]

The main unresolved risk is whether visitors can complete the whole journey independently and comfortably. Left-controller smooth movement and right-controller alternatives are not equivalent evidence of intuitive single-controller navigation. Existing welcome text promises seated/single-controller completion; that wording exceeds the present validation and should be qualified before release. Full narration, professional translation review, calibrated ergonomics and target-device performance are not established. [1,3,4]

RESET restores exhibit inspection state; RESET VIEW restores starting horizontal position and direction while retaining tracked eye height. Viewing-height adjustment is a preference, not floor calibration. The legacy NEW VISIT progress-clearing action is hidden in the default station, so staff handover between visitors still needs a verified procedure. For evaluation, restart sessions between participants or expose and verify an explicit operator reset. [4]

rows: Before submission
Use the packaged 6088c736 build to complete the core journey on PQ604 with the approved runtime.
Record headset/controller tracking, complete-flow outcome, hardware/runtime, errors and target-device performance.
Independent access
Enter, find controls, inspect and recover using a seated setup and one controller.
Completion, prompts, reach failures, unwanted movement, cancellation/recovery errors and discomfort.
Readable and credible learning
Read a component label, compare eras, use AIR/VOICE, then explain the physical relationship and reconstruction limits.
Observed reading/selection problems; explanation accuracy; confusion between historical fact and virtual teaching mechanisms.
Museum operation
Hide/recall the panel, recover a poor viewpoint, reset the exhibit and prepare for the next visitor.
Operator steps, residual selections/progress, failures to restore state and repeatability between sessions.

blocks.text: Agree the intended audience and success criteria before evaluation. Phase 3 should follow the course's external-participant, consent and anonymisation requirements, using observation and brief interviews alongside task outcomes. Compare the default interaction with an agreed alternative where feasible, analyse recurring problems, revise the prototype and repeat affected tasks. The existing visitor flags and assertion totals are unsuitable as learning or accessibility success measures. [2]

Historical accuracy remains bounded by references and estimated geometry; the full two-plinth scheme is still under review. Repository history separates original contributions from repairs and integration. Codex assisted implementation, model scripts, validation and this report; sources, known licences and assistance are recorded in the resource ledger. These records support inspection of the work, while user benefit remains an evaluation question. [6,11]
